name: AI incidents & governance
value: $129m deepfake fraud charges; EU draft law
summary: US charges three over a $129m deepfake executive fraud; EU readies draft rules on AI companion chatbots
state: US prosecutors unsealed charges on 5 Nov against three men accused of using AI-generated voice and video of chief executives and lawyers to steal about $129m from businesses between July 2024 and February 2026 (Biometric Update, 8 Nov). The European Commission is preparing a draft law, reported on 9 Nov, that would regulate AI chatbots designed to prolong engagement (Bloomberg). No AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure or AI-attributed mass harm had been found as of 10 Nov.
for_you: Fraud using cloned voices and video of executives is targeting staff who approve payments. The NCSC and Action Fraud advise verifying unusual payment requests through a separate, known channel.
rubric_hit: Significant AI misuse incident ($129m deepfake executive fraud charged 5 Nov); no critical-infrastructure attack

sources.title: Biometric Update — Deepfake CEOs, stolen lawyer identities fuel alleged $129M fraud
Bloomberg — EU targets addictive social media, AI chatbot features in draft law

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
